criteria.criterion: A listing seen for the first time has one InitialScrape history row with its price.
criteria.plannedImplementation: ListingUpserter.Apply adds a ListingStatusChangeEntity linked (via navigation, since the new listing has no Id yet) to every newly-inserted ListingEntity, with Source ListingHistorySource.InitialScrape, Status Active or Sold depending on listing.IsSold, and Price set to the listing's price.
criteria.plannedVerification: NewListingRecordsAnInitialScrapeHistoryRowTests.Should_record_exactly_one_initial_scrape_history_row_with_the_listings_price_for_a_new_listing upserts a brand-new listing through ScrapeStore against a real SQLite database and asserts exactly one ListingStatusChanges row exists for it, with Source InitialScrape and Price equal to the listing's price. Observable outcome: first-time scrape produces exactly one history row carrying the price.

criteria.criterion: Re-scraping at a different price updates Price and adds exactly one PriceUpdate row; re-scraping at the same price adds none.
criteria.plannedImplementation: ListingUpserter.Apply compares existing.Price to the incoming listing.Price before overwriting it; when they differ it adds a ListingStatusChangeEntity with Source ListingHistorySource.PriceUpdate and the new price, and adds nothing when they are equal.
criteria.plannedVerification: RescrapingAtANewPriceRecordsAPriceUpdateTests.Should_update_the_stored_price_and_add_exactly_one_price_update_row_when_rescraped_at_a_different_price upserts a listing twice at different prices and asserts the stored Price is the new value and exactly one PriceUpdate row exists. Should_add_no_additional_history_row_when_rescraped_at_the_same_price then upserts a third time at the same price and asserts the history row count is unchanged. Observable outcome: price history grows only when the price actually changes.

comparisonObservation.firstObservation: Upserting the same listing at a new price adds one PriceUpdate row and updates the stored Price.
comparisonObservation.whenHeldValueAbsent: Upserting the same listing again at the same price (the price delta absent) adds no further history row.

criteria.verificationStatus: verified: RescrapingAtANewPriceRecordsAPriceUpdateTests.Should_update_the_stored_price_and_add_exactly_one_price_update_row_when_rescraped_at_a_different_price and Should_add_no_additional_history_row_when_rescraped_at_the_same_price both passed against real SQLite

criteria.criterion: A refresh that observes a sale writes a StatusUpdate row with sold price and sold date.
criteria.plannedImplementation: ScrapeStore.RecordStatusChange adds a ListingStatusChangeEntity with Source ListingHistorySource.StatusUpdate whenever it records a status transition, carrying Price (preferring the observation's SoldPrice, then its Price, then the previously stored price) and SoldDateUtc from the merged listing.SoldDate.
criteria.plannedVerification: RefreshObservingASaleRecordsAStatusUpdateWithPriceAndSoldDateTests.Should_record_a_status_update_row_with_the_sold_price_and_sold_date_when_a_refresh_observes_a_sale seeds an active listing, calls RecordStatusChange with a sold observation carrying a sold price and sold date, and asserts the new history row has Source StatusUpdate, Price equal to the observed sold price and SoldDateUtc equal to the observed sold date. Observable outcome: a refresh that finds a sale leaves a history row a caller can use to reconstruct when and for how much the item sold.

criteria.criterion: Images, original price and category from a captured search payload are persisted; likes stays honestly unset because the real Mercari search payload never reports a like count.
criteria.plannedImplementation: MercariSearchPayloadParser.BuildSummary reads every photos[].imageUrl into ListingSummary.ImageUrls (and keeps the first as PrimaryImageUrl), originalPrice into OriginalPrice with the same cents-to-decimal conversion as price, and itemCategory.name into Category. Likes is passed through as null because grepping three real captured Mercari search payloads (search-active-ps5.json, search-sold-ps5.json, search-sold-ps5-100to200cents.json, 100+ items each) found zero occurrences of numLikes anywhere in the search API response — it is only present in the item-detail page's embedded Apollo cache, confirmed by finding "numLikes":32 in the captured item-active-m71344610988.html. ListingEntity gains a Likes column and ListingUpserter maps it so a future item-page detail fetch can populate it, but this ticket does not fabricate a value from search parsing. ListingUpserter serialises ImageUrls to JSON via ListingImageUrlsJson and ScrapeStore.GetListings deserialises it back.
criteria.plannedVerification: MercariSearchPayloadCarriesImagesOriginalPriceAndCategoryTests.Should_read_the_photo_url_original_price_and_category_from_a_captured_search_payload_item parses tests/MarketMakerEtl.Tests.Unit/Fixtures/Mercari/search-payload.json and asserts the first summary's ImageUrls equals ["https://u-mercari-images.mercdn.net/photos/m71344610988_1.jpg?1790200178"], OriginalPrice equals 399.00m and Category equals "Consoles". Should_leave_likes_unset_because_the_search_payload_never_reports_a_like_count asserts Likes is null for every parsed summary. ListingDetailFieldsRoundTripThroughTheStoreTests.Should_persist_image_urls_original_price_and_category_from_a_captured_search_payload_listing upserts that same parsed listing through ScrapeStore against real SQLite and asserts ImageUrls, OriginalPrice and Category read back unchanged. Observable outcome: every field the real payload actually carries survives persistence, and no field the payload lacks is invented.
materialConcerns: ticket-vs-reality gap: the ticket text says numLikes is already in the Mercari search payload but dropped; the real captures show it is not present in the search payload at all, only on the item-detail page. Documented as a gap rather than silently fabricating a Likes value from search data.
criteria.verificationStatus: verified: MercariSearchPayloadCarriesImagesOriginalPriceAndCategoryTests.Should_read_the_photo_url_original_price_and_category_from_a_captured_search_payload_item and Should_leave_likes_unset_because_the_search_payload_never_reports_a_like_count passed; ListingDetailFieldsRoundTripThroughTheStoreTests.Should_persist_image_urls_original_price_and_category_from_a_captured_search_payload_listing passed against real SQLite

criteria.criterion: Migrating a pre-change database keeps every listing and history row.
criteria.plannedImplementation: Migration 20260916000000_AddListingDetailAndPriceHistory only adds nullable columns to Listings (ShippingCost, Description, DescriptionStatus, ImageUrls, OriginalPrice, Category, Likes, PostedUtc, DetailFetchedUtc) and to ListingStatusChanges (Price, SoldDateUtc), plus a non-nullable Source column on ListingStatusChanges with a SQL-level default of 'StatusUpdate' so every pre-existing history row backfills as StatusUpdate without a data migration step; no column is dropped or renamed and no existing row is rewritten.
criteria.plannedVerification: MigratingAPreChangeDatabasePreservesListingsAndHistoryTests.Should_preserve_every_listing_and_history_row_when_migrating_a_pre_change_database seeds a database at the pre-change migration 20260915000000_AddListingBrand with a raw Listings row and a raw ListingStatusChanges row, applies migrations, and asserts: the Listings table now has a Category column and the ListingStatusChanges table now has a Source column; the legacy listing's Title and Price are unchanged; the legacy history row's Status is unchanged and its Source backfilled to StatusUpdate. Observable outcome: upgrading an existing database changes its shape without losing or corrupting any row.
materialConcerns: data loss: the test asserts the pre-existing listing and history row's values survive the migration byte-for-byte on the columns that existed before

comparisonObservation.firstObservation: A database created before this migration has a legacy listing and a legacy history row with no Source value.
comparisonObservation.whenHeldValueAbsent: After migrating, the same rows still exist with their original Title, Price and Status untouched, and the previously-absent Source column is present and backfilled rather than left null or dropping the row.

criteria.verificationStatus: verified: MigratingAPreChangeDatabasePreservesListingsAndHistoryTests.Should_preserve_every_listing_and_history_row_when_migrating_a_pre_change_database passed against real SQLite; migration renamed to 20260923234122_AddListingDetailAndPriceHistory and the test extended after rebasing onto main (see AC-11)

criteria.plannedImplementation: No production code implements this criterion directly; it constrains how AC-1 through AC-5 are tested.

criteria.criterion: Review fix: a search re-scrape must not erase enrichment fields (Likes, OriginalPrice, Category, ImageUrls, Condition, Brand, PrimaryImageUrl) the search endpoint never supplies.
criteria.plannedImplementation: ListingUpserter.UpdateExisting now splits field application into ApplyCoreSearchFields (Title, Currency, Url, IsSold, BuyingFormat: always applied; Price: only when the incoming value is non-null) and ApplyEnrichmentFields (Condition, PrimaryImageUrl, Brand, OriginalPrice, Category, Likes: null-coalesced onto the existing stored value so a null incoming value never overwrites a stored non-null value; ImageUrls: only replaced when the incoming list is non-empty). AddNew keeps a separate, fully unconditional ApplyNewListingFields since a freshly-inserted entity has nothing to preserve.
criteria.plannedVerification: SearchRescrapesPreserveEnrichmentFieldsTests.Should_keep_enrichment_fields_after_a_rescrape_whose_summary_has_them_null_or_empty seeds a listing with Likes=32, Brand, OriginalPrice, Category and two ImageUrls, then upserts a bare-bones re-scrape (Condition/PrimaryImageUrl/Brand null, no enrichment members set) and asserts every enrichment field is unchanged while Title and Price (both supplied) update. Verified red first: this test failed on the pre-fix ListingUpserter (all six enrichment assertions failed, ImageUrls null instead of the stored list) before the fix, then passed after. Observable outcome: a nightly search re-scrape cannot null out detail that only ticket #44's item-page fetch will ever populate.
criteria.verificationStatus: verified: SearchRescrapesPreserveEnrichmentFieldsTests.Should_keep_enrichment_fields_after_a_rescrape_whose_summary_has_them_null_or_empty passed against real SQLite; confirmed red against pre-fix ListingUpserter.cs

criteria.criterion: Review fix: a null incoming price must not be treated as a price change; it must leave the stored price unchanged and record no history row.
criteria.plannedImplementation: ListingUpserter.UpdateExisting computes priceChanged as listing.Price is not null && existing.Price != listing.Price, so a null incoming price never triggers the PriceUpdate branch and ApplyCoreSearchFields only assigns entity.Price when listing.Price is non-null.
criteria.plannedVerification: NullPriceOnRescrapeLeavesStoredPriceUnchangedTests.Should_leave_the_stored_price_unchanged_and_record_no_history_row_when_a_rescrape_reports_a_null_price seeds a listing at Price=100, re-upserts the same listing with Price=null, and asserts the stored price is still 100 and exactly one history row exists (the original InitialScrape row, no PriceUpdate row added). Verified red first: this test failed on the pre-fix ListingUpserter (stored price came back null and a second history row with Source PriceUpdate and a null price was present) before the fix, then passed after. Observable outcome: a parse miss on price can no longer wipe a known price or pollute price history with a null entry.
criteria.verificationStatus: verified: NullPriceOnRescrapeLeavesStoredPriceUnchangedTests.Should_leave_the_stored_price_unchanged_and_record_no_history_row_when_a_rescrape_reports_a_null_price passed against real SQLite; confirmed red against pre-fix ListingUpserter.cs

criteria.criterion: Review fix: a sold transition observed purely through search must set ItemStatus to Sold, write exactly one StatusUpdate history row with the sold price, set SoldPrice if unset, and must not duplicate the row when the listing is already sold.
criteria.plannedImplementation: ListingUpserter.UpdateExisting computes becameSold as !existing.IsSold && listing.IsSold before mutating; when true it sets existing.ItemStatus to Sold, backfills existing.SoldPrice with listing.Price only if SoldPrice was null, and calls the new shared AddHistoryRow helper with Source ListingHistorySource.StatusUpdate and Status Sold. Because becameSold is false once existing.IsSold is already true, re-observing an already-sold listing as sold again takes neither the sold-transition branch nor the price-changed branch when the price is unchanged, so no duplicate row is added.
criteria.plannedVerification: SearchObservingASaleTransitionRecordsAStatusUpdateTests.Should_record_a_status_update_row_and_mark_the_listing_sold_when_a_search_observes_the_sale_transition seeds an active listing at Price=85, re-upserts it as sold at the same price, and asserts ItemStatus is Sold, SoldPrice is 85, and exactly one StatusUpdate history row exists with Status Sold and Price 85. Should_not_duplicate_the_status_update_row_when_an_already_sold_listing_is_rescraped_as_sold_again then upserts the same already-sold listing a third time and asserts the StatusUpdate row count is still exactly one. Verified red first: both assertions failed on the pre-fix ListingUpserter (ItemStatus/SoldPrice stayed null/unset and no StatusUpdate row was ever written for a search-observed sale) before the fix, then passed after. Observable outcome: a nightly search that catches an item going from active to sold now leaves the same audit trail the old eBay job produced, without duplicating it on subsequent sold observations.
materialConcerns: judgment call: Currency and BuyingFormat were left as unconditional overwrites in ApplyCoreSearchFields (not added to the null-guarded enrichment set) because the coordinator's enrichment list did not name them and there is no live bug today — Mercari's parser always emits BuyingFormat: null (a no-op overwrite) and always supplies Currency. Flagged rather than silently deciding without visibility.

comparisonObservation.firstObservation: A search observing an already-stored active listing (IsSold=false) as sold (IsSold=true) sets ItemStatus to Sold, backfills SoldPrice, and writes one StatusUpdate history row.
comparisonObservation.whenHeldValueAbsent: A search observing an already-sold listing (IsSold=true) as sold again (the false-to-true transition absent) writes no additional history row and leaves ItemStatus/SoldPrice unchanged.

criteria.verificationStatus: verified: SearchObservingASaleTransitionRecordsAStatusUpdateTests.Should_record_a_status_update_row_and_mark_the_listing_sold_when_a_search_observes_the_sale_transition and Should_not_duplicate_the_status_update_row_when_an_already_sold_listing_is_rescraped_as_sold_again both passed against real SQLite; confirmed red against pre-fix ListingUpserter.cs

criteria.criterion: Rebase fix: after #40 (job scheduling/categories) and #42 (Mercari item-page parsing) merged to main, this branch's migration must be reordered to apply after #40's real migration, generated via EF tooling rather than hand-written, and a full migration from a #40-era database must still preserve jobs, runs, listings and categories.
criteria.plannedImplementation: Deleted the hand-written 20260916000000_AddListingDetailAndPriceHistory migration and its Designer file, reset EtlDbContextModelSnapshot.cs to main's version, then ran dotnet ef migrations add AddListingDetailAndPriceHistory --project src/MarketMakerEtl.Core --startup-project src/MarketMakerEtl.Api, which discovers EtlDbContext through the DbContextOptions<EtlDbContext> that AddDbContextFactory registers in DI (no IDesignTimeDbContextFactory needed, contrary to the AC-5 gap's original assumption). The regenerated migration is 20260923234122_AddListingDetailAndPriceHistory, ordered after #40's 20260923231305_AddJobSchedulingAndCategories. Hand-edited only to add the // <auto-generated /> header and internal accessibility (matching every other migration; raw dotnet ef output was public with no header) and to change the generated Source column's backfill defaultValue from "" to "StatusUpdate", preserving the original migration's backfill intent.
criteria.plannedVerification: Rebased feat/43-listing-detail-and-price-history onto origin/main twice (conflict-free both times, since #40 and #42 touch no file this ticket owns). dotnet ef migrations list and dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes confirm the new migration is ordered after #40's and the model has no pending changes. MigratingAPreChangeDatabasePreservesListingsAndHistoryTests was extended to seed a job, run, listing, category and job-category link at #40's migration point (20260923231305_AddJobSchedulingAndCategories) via raw SQL, then call ApplyMigrations to head, and assert the job's SearchTerm/IntervalHours, the run's SearchTerm, the category's Name and the job-category link, plus the pre-existing listing/history row and its Source backfill, all survive. Observable outcome: upgrading a database that already has #40's schema through this ticket's migration does not corrupt or drop any of #40's data.
materialConcerns: While re-running the full suite after the rebase, MercariItemPageParsesActiveItemDetailsTests and MercariItemPageReportsSoldItemTests (both owned by #42, no file this ticket touches) failed. Confirmed via a clean git archive of origin/main that this is pre-existing on main itself on this Windows machine, not introduced by the rebase: their expected description constants are C# 11 raw string literals, and Roslyn normalizes a raw string literal's embedded line endings to the host OS's newline at compile time (CRLF on Windows) regardless of the source file's own line endings, while the fixture's JSON payload always encodes literal \n. This blocked the shared pre-commit gate for every commit on this branch, so it needed fixing to proceed. Fixed minimally by appending .ReplaceLineEndings("\n") to both constants (const string to static readonly string, since const can't call an instance method) so the compiled value is deterministic across platforms and matches the parser's actual, correct output; #42's parser itself was not touched.
